name: PaperBench
intro: PaperBench 评测智能体从零复现前沿 AI 研究的能力。它包含 20 篇 ICML 2024 Spotlight/Oral 论文和 8,316 个分层叶节点，候选者提交带 reproduce.sh 的代码仓库，在全新环境执行后由 SimpleJudge 逐叶节点评分并加权汇总。
build_method: 论文筛选, 双工程师分层rubric, 原作者多轮核验, JudgeEval验证
eval_feature: 全新Ubuntu 24.04环境, A10 GPU, 12小时复现实验, SimpleJudge逐叶节点判定, 加权树聚合
scale: 20篇论文, 12个ICML主题, 8,316个叶节点评分结果
build_method_en: Paper filtering, two-engineer hierarchical rubrics, multi-round author verification, JudgeEval validation
eval_feature_en: Fresh Ubuntu 24.04 VM, A10 GPU, 12-hour reproduction, per-leaf SimpleJudge decisions, weighted tree aggregation
intro_en: PaperBench evaluates agents' ability to replicate frontier AI research from scratch. It contains 20 ICML 2024 Spotlight/Oral papers and 8,316 hierarchical leaves; candidates submit a repository with reproduce.sh, which is executed in a fresh environment before SimpleJudge grades every leaf and weighted scores roll up to the root.

drawio_review_note: reviewed_at=2026-07-22; source_scope=paper-v3 plus immutable official code-and-data release. PAPER: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.01848v3 and https://arxiv.org/pdf/2504.01848v3. arXiv identifies v3 as the 2025-04-07 revision. The downloaded v3 PDF has SHA-256 2f58f1a6581af9d99432422dccf3cf61f5c263377c1e4550e7333c4a22d7184d. FIXED CODE/DATA: https://github.com/openai/frontier-evals/tree/df37a1752ad6b091e223e75606c51aacab4215a5/project/paperbench. Commit df37a1752ad6b091e223e75606c51aacab4215a5 is the official 2025-04-08 correction that adds the missing stochastic-interpolants data and self-composing-policies to the development split. Its repository root tree is d479c0631377281837350179e5dd9f5fbc120702, PaperBench project tree is caec0bdac8e6c8a29a0df88d4ff9d9fc5a7ccf83, and data tree is b5d175101d5b5054748529004c5c0f9acf260654. The fixed README SHA-256 is f47ca01e9e721cdfe93cec7044f967adc7771232f6a87ef9030734e5d9db4733; the all split SHA-256 is f2b382a46499f0c6801e7b62b171d8616f7be228c118c9756ce02a19f5ec5348; judge.py SHA-256 is 4159fa156f4f21af68ecd6bc1fb5b0be31ad5851985c328a8def2505d58ec5b2; metrics.py SHA-256 is 88a0254c33ecee1066101809af611e21f31688f2d473d466794f6892d2c2342f. PAPER SELECTION: Appendix B starts from ICML 2024 Spotlight and Oral papers. gpt-4o-2024-08-06 performs initial filtering. The commercial/geographic filter excludes papers unlikely to support author collaboration under the disclosed affiliation threshold. The empirical filter requires a substantial experiment with non-trivial engineering and excludes pure theory or work primarily introducing frameworks, libraries, or tools. Hardware filtering removes work requiring distributed multi-node training. Model-dependency filtering excludes reliance on closed pretrained models such as GPT-4, Claude, or PaLM. Data filtering excludes new human collection or annotation. Reproducibility filtering requires enough methodological detail to reproduce from the paper. Accessible-dependency filtering requires dependencies to be obtainable, substitutable, or droppable without making the task uninteresting. The team randomly reads survivors to catch missed issues, contacts authors until 42 have been approached, and secures 20 author collaborations covering 12 ICML topics. RUBRIC CONSTRUCTION: two research engineers deeply read each selected paper and draft the initial rubric. The rubric is a tree: children decompose the parent outcome; leaf criteria are continuously refined until an expert familiar with the paper should be able to decide one in under 15 minutes. All nodes are weighted by importance relative to siblings, not implementation difficulty. Across the 20 benchmark papers the paper reports 8,316 leaves. Leaves have three paper-defined requirement types: Code Development, Execution, and Result Match. Several internal review rounds refine structure and wording. One original author then works under a formal agreement through multiple feedback rounds to verify correctness and give final approval. Clarifications and out-of-scope items enter a candidate-facing addendum; where necessary a separate judge-only addendum provides grading reference information. The public fixed release contains paper PDF and Markdown, addendum, assets, rubric.json, blacklist.txt, config.yaml, and optional judge.addendum.md. RELEASE RECONCILIATION: initial official release commit 352ed048d510a2525aea658489b3839b4efc412b had 22 paper folders while all.txt referenced stochastic-interpolants without its data, and the dev split had only semantic-self-consistency and self-expansion. The pinned corrective commit df37a1752ad6b091e223e75606c51aacab4215a5 has 23 paper folders and 23 rubrics: 20 IDs in experiments/splits/all.txt plus three development IDs semantic-self-consistency, self-expansion, and self-composing-policies. It also contains the debug split rice, a five-paper human split, and five JudgeEval example directories. This correction is why the detail URL does not pin the incomplete initial commit. The project inherits the root MIT LICENSE.md; no separate Hugging Face dataset is used. CANDIDATE ACCESS AND RULES: the evaluated candidate receives the paper, author clarification addendum, and instructions, but does not see the rubric during the attempt. The candidate may browse the internet but cannot use the original authors' codebases or any site in the per-paper blacklist. A post-hoc monitor searches logs for blacklisted URLs and escalates hits for manual disqualification. The candidate must submit a repository with all code and a root reproduce.sh entrypoint. The paper's main experiments run each agent in Ubuntu 24.04 with one NVIDIA A10 and a maximum 12-hour agent runtime. REPRODUCTION: after the attempt, the submission is copied to a fresh Ubuntu 24.04 VM with one A10. reproduce.sh is executed from a clean start; the paper caps this phase at 12 hours and reports average agent-produced script runtime of 5.5 minutes. The updated directory, generated files, and reproduce.log form the executed submission. Separating reproduction from rollout makes hard-coded task-time artifacts distinguishable from cleanly regenerated results. GRADING: SimpleJudge independently grades every leaf. It sees paper Markdown, the full rubric, addenda, the target requirement, prior siblings and ancestors, and requirement-relevant submission evidence. For Code Development and Execution nodes it whitelists documentation, source, and configuration files; for Result Match it focuses on documentation and table-like files created or modified during reproduction. If all relevant content does not fit, it asks the judge to rank file names and includes the top ten files within the remaining context budget. Code Development asks whether correct code exists and can inspect docs, source, and reproduce.sh. Execution additionally uses reproduce.log to ask whether the required execution occurred. Result Match uses reproduce.sh, reproduce.log, and newly generated outputs to ask whether evidence agrees with the paper. A missing reproduce.sh forces Execution and Result Match leaves to zero. Unless otherwise stated, the paper uses o3-mini-2025-01-31 with reasoning effort high. Each leaf is binary: 1 fulfilled, 0 unfulfilled. A parent score is the weighted mean of child scores; propagation reaches the root, producing the submission Replication Score. The main benchmark metric is average Replication Score over all 20 papers, with three runs per paper in the main experiments. JUDGEEVAL: the auxiliary judge benchmark is an independent branch, not part of every PaperBench run. It uses partial replications of four PaperBench papers plus one development paper, created from scratch or by modifying authors' repositories. Experts manually grade all relevant rubric leaves and preserve binary scores and explanations as gold. JudgeEval does not run reproduce.sh; examples are treated as already being in their post-reproduction state. It evaluates GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o, o1-mini, o1, and o3-mini with accuracy, precision, recall, and F1, macro-averaged across papers. The paper reports o3-mini SimpleJudge F1 0.83 at about USD 66 per paper. CODE-DEV BOUNDARY: PaperBench Code-Dev skips reproduction and grades only Code Development leaves. It is cheaper and more accessible but explicitly less rigorous and only weakly correlated with the full benchmark, so the diagram marks it as a dashed variant boundary rather than merging it into the main flow. PAPER/RELEASE DRIFT: the paper's historical 12-hour A10 setup is the main semantic contract represented in the diagram. Later repository revisions add newer agents and longer canonical examples; those later operational examples do not rewrite the paper's benchmark-construction and evaluation claims. LANGUAGE/TOPOLOGY REVIEW: the EN and ZH specs have identical semantic IDs, node types, sizes, coordinates, edges, and dashed-secondary markers. They separately show paper selection, author-approved rubric creation, hidden-candidate access, clean reproduction, the three grading branches, context filtering, SimpleJudge, weighted score propagation, independent JudgeEval, corrective release pin, and Code-Dev boundary. No unavailable rubric, author-code access, or implicit reproduction result is invented. Formal publication evidence [site-a12d-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 3533×1545 (English) and 3533×1545 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 3531×1543 and 3531×1543. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
